note: Recast from the original description of the new species by Snyder 1952 (in English), published as Rugitermes unicolor sp. n., type locality Sahacéc, Alta Vera Paz, Guatemala, typical lowland rainforest; described from 4 alates (2 males and 2 females, collected in 1951, month 5 (May) by G. Becker, reared in the laboratory from nymphs) and 2 soldiers. The alate is not accompanied by measurements, only a qualitative description and the venation. This is the northernmost American record of the genus. Some rows of the original measurement table are out of order in the scan and only the legible rows are entered.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate is unicolorous rather than bicolorous: the head is yellowish brown and the pronotum yellow, clearly unlike the bicolorous pattern of the closely related R. bicolor and its allies, with a dark head and a yellow pronotum; the wings are dark brown to almost black and coarsely punctate. The soldier is smaller and paler than in R. costaricensis, and the pronotum shape also differs (in the latter it is more angular, body length 10—12.5 mm, antenna 15 segments).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Alate: head yellowish brown, smooth, shiny, longer than wide, the sides rounded, with fairly dense long and short hairs. Postclypeus white, tinged yellow. Labrum pale yellowish brown, with long hairs. Eyes black, not round, projecting, the distance to the lateral margin of the head about equal to the eye diameter. Ocelli transparent, nearly oval, at an oblique angle to the eye, slightly more than one ocellus long diameter from the eye. Antenna pale yellowish brown, becoming white towards the tip, 16—17 segments, segment 3 longer than segments 2 and 4. Pronotum yellow, 2 times as wide as long, the anterior and posterior margins shallowly concave, the sides rounded, narrowing posteriorly, with scattered long hairs. Wings dark brown to almost black, coarsely punctate; the media of the forewing is connected almost directly to the radial sector, the radial sector lies close to and parallel to the costa and has 6 branches; the cubitus lies above the middle of the wing, parallel to the radial sector, with 10 branches reaching the wing margin; in the hindwing the media is absent, the radial sector has 2 long and 2 short branches reaching the costa, and the cubitus lies above the middle of the wing with 10 branches reaching the wing margin. Legs nearly black to yellowish brown. Abdominal tergites yellow, with long dense hairs near the base.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Soldier: mandibles black; the distal 1/3 of the left mandible has two marginal teeth, one smaller tooth and a molar; the right mandible has two larger marginal teeth, one at the middle and one near the base. Antenna yellow, 13 segments, segment 3 yellowish brown, longer than segment 2 and almost equal to segments 4 and 5 together. Pronotum yellow, kidney-shaped, more than 2 times as wide as long, the anterior and posterior margins shallowly concave, the sides narrowing posteriorly, with dense long and short hairs. Legs tinged yellow, hairy, the femora swollen. Abdominal tergites pale yellow, each with a row of long hairs at its base. Measurements (mm): total soldier length 7.60—8.00; head length including the mandibles 3.50—3.65; mean head length (to the anterior margin) 2.43; hind tibia length 0.95; head width 1.80; pronotum width 1.80. The values for left mandible length and pronotum length are displaced in the scanned measurement table and cannot be read, and are not entered.
